newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ sees evidence of positive Japan economic cycle.
newsitem.headline: BOJ sees evidence of positive Japan economic cycle.

text.p: Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a news conference on Wednesday that there was evidence that a positive economic cycle was under way in the Japanese economy based on private-sector demand.
Matsushita said positive cyclical mechanisms in which higher corporate profits and an increase in personal income were leading to increases in consumption and production were becoming recognisable.
"The economy is continuing its gradual recovery and the the recovery is becoming more solid," he said.

Matsushita said production was growing at quite a rapid pace. However, he added that market participants were still cautious about the economy and this was reflected in the stock market and in long-term interest rates.
"We still need to determine the effect of stock price falls on sentiment," he said.

He said that although the economy may become sluggish in the first part of the fiscal year from April 1 due to a scheduled increase in Japan"s consumption tax, the recent strength of private-sector demand suggested there was a good possibility that the economic recovery would continue.
"Our monetary policy for now is to secure a basis for further economic recovery while keeping close watch over (economic) developments," he said.

Matsushita said the issue of problem loans at Japanese banks was being addressed steadily by the financial institutions. However, he stressed the need for banks to strengthen their management through restructuring efforts and for them to boost their assets while keeping in mind the effect of fals in stock prices.
"We will encourage financial firms" restructuring efforts. Should they face liquidity problems in the process, the Bank of Japan will do what it can to support them," Matsushita said.
He added that the central bank would also take appropriate measures to ensure stability in the financial system.
